items.requirement: Confirm whether the organisation processes digital personal data within India or processes digital personal data outside India in connection with offering goods or services to Data Principals in India.
items.guardrail: DPDPA applies to digital personal data, not every form of business data. Anonymised or non-personal business data should be assessed separately.

items.requirement: Identify whether the organisation acts as a Data Fiduciary, Data Processor, Consent Manager, or another relevant participant.
items.guardrail: The primary accountability sits with the Data Fiduciary. Processors act on behalf of the Data Fiduciary.

items.requirement: Check whether the organisation or class of organisations has been notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary by the Central Government.
items.guardrail: Do not assume SDF status. Additional SDF obligations apply only where notified.

items.requirement: Process personal data only for a lawful purpose and in accordance with the Act.
items.guardrail: "Business convenience" is not enough. Purpose must be lawful and specific.

items.requirement: Map every processing activity to either valid consent or a permitted legitimate use under the Act.
items.guardrail: Do not stretch legitimate use. Use it only where the Act permits it.

items.requirement: Provide notice before or along with the request for consent, describing the personal data and the purpose of processing.
items.guardrail: A generic privacy policy alone may not be enough where a specific consent notice is required.

items.requirement: For consent obtained before commencement, provide notice as soon as reasonably practicable.
items.guardrail: Legacy consent clean-up is essential. Old databases often have weak consent evidence.

items.requirement: Give the Data Principal the option to access the notice in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
items.guardrail: Especially important for consumer-facing websites, apps, and public platforms.

items.requirement: Notice should be clear, plain, independently understandable, and include itemised personal data, processing purpose, withdrawal mechanism, rights mechanism, and complaint path to the Board. The notified Rules prescribe this structure.
items.guardrail: Avoid burying notice inside unrelated legal text. The notice must stand on its own.

items.requirement: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous, given through clear affirmative action, and limited to personal data necessary for the specified purpose.
items.guardrail: No pre-ticked boxes. No bundled consent. No consent traps.

items.requirement: Any consent term that violates the Act, Rules, or another applicable law is invalid to that extent.
items.guardrail: Do not insert waiver clauses that dilute Data Principal rights.

items.requirement: Consent requests must be in clear and plain language and include contact details of the DPO or authorised person, where applicable.
items.guardrail: Legalese is camouflage, not compliance.

items.requirement: Allow withdrawal of consent at any time, with ease comparable to giving consent. After withdrawal, the Data Fiduciary must cease processing within a reasonable time unless continued processing is authorised by law.
items.guardrail: Withdrawal must propagate to processors, downstream systems, and campaign lists.

items.requirement: Where consent is the basis of processing, the Data Fiduciary must be able to prove that notice was given and consent was obtained in accordance with the Act and Rules.
items.guardrail: Maintain consent timestamp, purpose, notice version, user/channel details, and withdrawal logs.

items.requirement: If acting as or using a Consent Manager, comply with registration and prescribed technical, operational, financial, and fiduciary requirements.
items.guardrail: Do not casually label a consent tool as a "Consent Manager" unless it meets regulated requirements.

items.requirement: Process data for the specified purpose for which the Data Principal voluntarily provided personal data, where applicable.
items.guardrail: Voluntary provision is not a blank cheque. Keep processing tied to the stated purpose.

items.requirement: Processing may be permitted for certain State functions, benefits, subsidies, certificates, licences, or permits.
items.guardrail: Mostly relevant to government and public-sector contexts.

items.subsection: 5.3 Medical emergency, disaster, epidemic, public safety
items.requirement: Processing may be permitted for specified emergency, disaster, epidemic, or public safety situations.
items.guardrail: Document the emergency basis. Do not use emergency provisions for routine processing.

items.requirement: Processing may be permitted for employment purposes and safeguarding the employer from loss or liability, where covered.
items.guardrail: HR data is still personal data. Apply purpose limitation, access control, and retention discipline.

items.requirement: The Data Fiduciary is responsible for complying with the Act for processing undertaken by it or on its behalf.
items.guardrail: Outsourcing processing does not outsource accountability.

items.requirement: Engage a Data Processor only under a valid contract.
items.guardrail: Vendor Data Processing Agreements are mandatory hygiene.

items.requirement: Ensure completeness, accuracy, and consistency where personal data is used to make decisions or disclosed to another Data Fiduciary.
items.guardrail: Highly relevant for KYC, credit, payroll, collections, support, and employee records.

items.requirement: Implement reasonable security safeguards, including controls such as access control, encryption, masking, obfuscation, tokenisation, logging, monitoring, backups, and breach detection where applicable.
items.guardrail: Keep technical evidence: policies, configurations, audit logs, access reports, backup reports, incident records.

items.requirement: Notify the Data Protection Board and affected Data Principals of personal data breaches in the prescribed manner.
items.guardrail: Breach SOP must support rapid assessment, notification, impact analysis, remediation, and evidence preservation.

items.subsection: 6.6 Erasure after purpose completion or withdrawal
items.requirement: Erase personal data when consent is withdrawn or the specified purpose is no longer served, unless retention is necessary for legal compliance.
items.guardrail: Deletion must cover source systems, processors, archives, exports, and downstream platforms.

items.requirement: Publish contact details of the DPO or authorised person and provide an effective grievance redressal mechanism.
items.guardrail: Rule 13 workflows should be tracked against the maximum response period of 90 days.

title: Children's Data and Persons with Disability

items.requirement: Obtain verifiable parental consent before processing personal data of a child.
items.guardrail: Under the Act, a child means a person below 18 years of age.

items.requirement: Obtain verifiable consent of the lawful guardian where applicable for persons with disability.
items.guardrail: Apply only where Rule conditions are met.

items.requirement: Do not undertake tracking, behavioural monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children.
items.guardrail: Product, analytics, and ad-tech teams must implement technical controls. Policy text alone is not enough.

items.requirement: Do not process children's personal data in a manner likely to cause detrimental effect on child wellbeing.
items.guardrail: Run child-risk review before launching child-facing features.

items.requirement: Check whether any notified exemption applies for specific classes of Data Fiduciaries or purposes.
items.guardrail: Do not self-declare exemption. Verify the notification or rule basis.

items.requirement: If notified as an SDF, appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India.
items.guardrail: Useful for many organisations, but mandatory under DPDPA only where SDF obligations apply.

items.requirement: If notified as an SDF, appoint an independent data auditor.
items.guardrail: Maintain audit scope, report, findings, remediation tracker, and management sign-off.

items.subsection: 8.3 DPIA, periodic audit, and additional measures
items.requirement: If notified as an SDF, conduct DPIA, periodic audit, and prescribed compliance measures.
items.guardrail: DPIA is a statutory SDF control, not a universal DPDPA obligation for every organisation.

items.subsection: 8.4 Restrictions for notified categories of data
items.requirement: If applicable to an SDF, comply with Central Government requirements or restrictions relating to notified categories of personal data and traffic data.
items.guardrail: Do not describe this as general "data localisation" under DPDPA. DPDPA follows a negative-list model for cross-border transfers. Localisation may arise from sectoral laws or specific notifications, not as a blanket DPDPA mandate.

items.requirement: Provide a mechanism for Data Principals to obtain information about personal data processing and sharing, as applicable.
items.guardrail: Maintain request intake, identity verification, response template, fulfilment evidence, and SLA tracker. Rule 13 workflows should not exceed 90 days.

items.requirement: Enable Data Principals to request correction, completion, updating, and erasure of personal data.
items.guardrail: Track request date, system owner, fulfilment date, exception reason, and closure evidence. Rule 13 workflows should not exceed 90 days.

items.requirement: Provide readily available means of grievance redressal.
items.guardrail: The Data Principal should normally exhaust this mechanism before escalating to the Board.

items.requirement: Enable a Data Principal to nominate another person to exercise rights in the event of death or incapacity.
items.guardrail: Collect only necessary nominee details and verify before fulfilment.

items.requirement: Data Principals must comply with applicable laws while exercising rights.
items.guardrail: Useful for handling fraudulent, abusive, or impersonation-based requests.

items.requirement: Data Principals must not impersonate another person or suppress material information.
items.guardrail: Include identity verification in rights workflows.

items.requirement: Personal data may be transferred outside India except to countries or territories restricted by Central Government notification.
items.guardrail: This is a negative-list model, not a blanket localisation requirement. Maintain a transfer register and monitor restricted-country notifications.

items.requirement: Check whether stricter sectoral laws, regulatory directions, contracts, or government notifications impose additional transfer or localisation requirements.
items.guardrail: RBI, telecom, insurance, health, payments, tax, and employment rules may impose separate requirements.
items.reference: Act Sec. 16 and other applicable laws

items.requirement: Identify whether processing is exempt, such as personal or domestic processing.
items.guardrail: Enterprise processing should not casually rely on domestic-use exemptions.

items.requirement: Processing may be exempt for research, archival, or statistical purposes if not used to make decisions specific to a Data Principal and if done according to prescribed standards.
items.guardrail: Use output controls, de-identification, and purpose restrictions.

items.subsection: 12.3 Legal, court, enforcement, and State exemptions
items.requirement: Check exemptions for legal claims, courts, enforcement, security, sovereignty, and other statutory purposes.
items.guardrail: Keep legal sign-off. These exemptions are context-specific.

items.requirement: Prepare for Board notices, inquiries, directions, digital proceedings, and compliance interactions.
items.guardrail: Maintain response owner, evidence pack, legal escalation matrix, and management reporting.

items.requirement: Track penalty exposure for breach of obligations including security safeguards, breach notification, children's data obligations, SDF obligations, Consent Manager obligations, and Data Principal duties.
items.guardrail: The Act's penalty factors are in Section 33(2), not Section 33(3). The power to amend the Schedule, with a cap that an amount must not exceed more than twice the original amount, appears under Section 42.

items.requirement: Track phased commencement of DPDP Rules: Rules 1, 2, and 17–21 from publication; Rule 4 after one year; Rules 3, 5–16, 22, and 23 after eighteen months.
items.guardrail: Maintain a compliance roadmap by effective date, not just by policy priority.

items.requirement: Maintain a system-wise register of personal data collected, stored, processed, shared, archived, and deleted.
items.guardrail: Do not call this a GDPR RoPA unless your policy defines it. Use "DPDPA Processing Register."

items.requirement: Map each activity to purpose, data category, Data Principal category, lawful basis, owner, processor, retention, and transfer location.
items.guardrail: This prevents "mystery processing." Mystery is fun in novels, not audits.

items.requirement: Document flow from collection to storage, use, sharing, archival, deletion, and processor handoff.
items.guardrail: Include SaaS tools, APIs, data lake, BI reports, logs, backups, and exports.

items.requirement: Maintain notice versions, publication date, language versions, purpose mapping, approval record, and publishing channel.
items.guardrail: Proves what was shown to the Data Principal at the time of consent.

items.requirement: Capture user ID, consent timestamp, purpose, notice version, channel, language, consent status, and withdrawal status.
items.guardrail: Consent without evidence is just a bedtime story.

items.requirement: Track withdrawal request, date, systems affected, processor notification, cessation confirmation, and exceptions.
items.guardrail: Withdrawal must not die in the website front end.

items.requirement: Identify pre-commencement consents and issue required notices where applicable.
items.guardrail: Old databases usually carry the highest consent risk.

items.requirement: Define SOP for access, correction, completion, update, erasure, grievance, and nomination requests.
items.guardrail: Include identity verification, request classification, SLA tracking, and exception handling.

items.requirement: Track request date, request type, identity check, owner, response date, closure evidence, and pending ageing.
items.guardrail: Configure dashboard alerts before the 90-day maximum is breached.

items.requirement: Maintain deletion tickets, database confirmation, processor deletion certificate, exception note, and legal-hold record.
items.guardrail: Erasure is a chain, not a button.

items.requirement: Maintain nomination capture, verification, trigger event process, and fulfilment records.
items.guardrail: Avoid over-collecting nominee data.

items.requirement: Map each system to encryption, masking, tokenisation, RBAC, MFA, PAM, logging, monitoring, DLP, backup, and DR controls.
items.guardrail: Technical safeguards need technical proof.

items.requirement: Conduct periodic access certification for HRMS, CRM, ERP, support tools, data lake, BI tools, and production databases.
items.guardrail: Privileged access is where privacy often goes to die. Review it.

items.requirement: Maintain SIEM alerts, access logs, anomaly detection evidence, and incident tickets.
items.guardrail: Logs must be retained according to security policy and applicable law.

items.requirement: Maintain backup reports, restore test results, DR test evidence, and resilience review.
items.guardrail: A backup never restored is only a prayer with a timestamp.

items.requirement: Maintain VA/PT reports, patch tickets, risk acceptance, exception approvals, and closure evidence.
items.guardrail: Prioritise systems holding personal data.

items.requirement: Define detection, classification, escalation, containment, legal review, Board notification, Data Principal notification, RCA, and remediation.
items.guardrail: Must support prescribed breach notification duties.

items.requirement: Maintain breach evidence template: facts, timeline, affected data, impact, containment, mitigation, and remedial actions.
items.guardrail: Start tracking from awareness. Do not spend three days arguing over definitions.

items.requirement: Maintain breach ID, detection date, awareness date, systems affected, data impacted, notification status, RCA, and closure.
items.guardrail: Track near-misses separately for learning.

items.requirement: Conduct tabletop exercises and retain minutes, observations, and action tracker.
items.guardrail: The first breach drill should not happen during the breach.

items.requirement: List all Data Processors and third parties receiving or processing personal data.
items.guardrail: Include SaaS, cloud, payroll, call centre, analytics, marketing, and support tools.

items.requirement: Include purpose limitation, confidentiality, security safeguards, breach reporting, subprocessor control, deletion, audit, and liability clauses.
items.guardrail: Vendor contracts must mirror the accountability model of DPDPA.

items.requirement: Maintain due diligence questionnaire, security certifications, risk score, remediation plan, and approval record.
items.guardrail: High-risk vendors need stronger controls and shorter review cycles.

items.requirement: Obtain deletion certificate or system evidence after purpose closure, consent withdrawal, or contract termination.
items.guardrail: "We emailed the vendor" is not proof.

items.requirement: Define retention period by data category: customer, employee, vendor, finance, tax, logs, tickets, recordings, and app data.
items.guardrail: Align with company law, tax law, labour law, sectoral rules, and legal-hold requirements.

items.requirement: Define when data must be retained for legal claim, litigation, investigation, statutory requirement, or regulatory process.
items.guardrail: Legal hold can override deletion, but it must be documented.

items.requirement: Maintain disposal logs, deletion scripts, archival purge reports, and media destruction certificates.
items.guardrail: Retention without deletion is data obesity.

items.requirement: Implement age declaration, verification method, parental consent trigger, and child-user handling.
items.guardrail: Avoid collecting children's data unless genuinely required.

items.requirement: Maintain parent/guardian verification evidence according to the approved mechanism.
items.guardrail: Keep it proportionate and privacy-preserving.

items.requirement: Disable behavioural tracking, profiling, and targeted advertising directed at children.
items.guardrail: Product, analytics, and ad-tech implementation must match policy.

items.requirement: Maintain periodic assessment of whether the organisation is notified as an SDF.
items.guardrail: Re-check government notifications periodically.

items.requirement: Maintain DPO appointment letter, India contact details, reporting line, and responsibility charter.
items.guardrail: Mandatory for SDFs; useful governance for larger non-SDF organisations too.

items.requirement: Maintain DPIA template, completed DPIAs, risk ratings, mitigation plan, and approval record.
items.guardrail: Do not call every risk note a DPIA. Use a structured assessment.

items.requirement: Maintain audit scope, audit report, findings, remediation tracker, and management sign-off.
items.guardrail: Make findings visible to senior management.

items.requirement: Maintain destination country, recipient, data category, purpose, contract reference, and safeguard details.
items.guardrail: Track restricted countries or territories if notified by the Central Government.

items.requirement: Map RBI, IRDAI, TRAI, telecom, health, tax, employment, and contractual restrictions where applicable.
items.guardrail: DPDPA is not the only law in the room.

items.requirement: Train IT, HR, marketing, customer support, procurement, product, legal, and leadership teams.
items.guardrail: Generic privacy training is weak. Role-based training is sharper.
items.reference: Supports Act Sec. 8; Rule 6, Rule 7, Rule 13

items.requirement: Maintain attendance, quiz scores, acknowledgement, refresher schedule, and training material versions.
items.guardrail: Auditors love proof. Employees love forgetting. Keep records.

items.requirement: Report consent gaps, rights requests, grievances, breaches, vendor risks, deletion backlog, SDF actions, and exceptions.
items.guardrail: What leadership cannot see, leadership cannot govern.

items.requirement: Track exceptions, risk owner, mitigation, due date, approval, and expiry.
items.guardrail: Permanent exceptions are policy sabotage.

items.requirement: Prepare quarterly privacy compliance reporting for leadership or the board.
items.guardrail: Especially important for regulated, high-volume, or consumer-facing businesses.
